review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the uses of the simp-related lemmas. The sibling file P2M/Sol/S_WeierstrassCurve_exists_variableChange_of_comp_eq_id_of_mem_rationalHomSet.lean has the same declarations. I checked Mathlib's `map` (`@[simps]`) and `baseChange` (a plain `def`) in Weierstrass.lean. The scoped simp lemmas `substXY_*`, `bc_CC`, `bc_CX` and `bc_Y` look fine. I found no loop. I could not run Lean, so I don't claim any observed simp behaviour. The findings are about missing or inconsistent simp coverage. The `vcOf` finding is the strongest. The other two are weaker.

findings.excerpt: theorem vcOf_r (μ r σ t : F) (hμ : μ ≠ 0) : (vcOf μ r σ t hμ).r = -r / μ ^ 2 := rfl
findings.problem: These four lemmas are the projection lemmas for the def `vcOf`. They are the canonical normal forms for `(vcOf ..).u⁻¹`, `.r`, `.s` and `.t`. None of them is a simp lemma, so every use needs a hand-written `rw`, as in `vcOf_substX` and `vcOf_substY`. `vcOf_smul_eq` instead uses `unfold vcOf` followed by the extra helper `hu`. `main` repeats `(vcOf (β₀ / α₀) r₀ σ₀ t₀ hμ)` many times in `hX`, `hY` and `hns`, and none of that can be simplified.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `vcOf_u_inv`, `vcOf_r`, `vcOf_s` and `vcOf_t` as `@[simp]`, or `@[scoped simp]` like the other lemmas in this development. The right-hand sides contain no `vcOf`, so this cannot cycle. Then `vcOf_substX` and `vcOf_substY` can start with `simp only [vcOf_u_inv, vcOf_r, ...]` and the `rw` list can go. In `vcOf_smul_eq` the `unfold vcOf` and `hu` can be replaced by the simp lemmas.
findings.benefit: The projections of `vcOf` then normalise automatically, and the repeated `rw [vcOf_u_inv, vcOf_r, vcOf_s, vcOf_t]` and `unfold vcOf` workarounds disappear.

findings.excerpt: theorem baseChange_a₁ : (W.baseChange k).a₁ = ι W.a₁ := rfl
findings.problem: `WeierstrassCurve.baseChange` is a plain `def` in Mathlib, so Mathlib's `@[simps]` lemmas `map_a₁`, … do not fire on `(W.baseChange k).a₁`. These five lemmas are the missing simp lemmas for that case. They are declared without any simp attribute and are never used in the file. Instead, `descent` proves `hℓ` and `hc` by hand to evaluate `(W.baseChange k).toAffine.a₁` and the other coefficients. `exists_bc_eq_linear` and `equation_iff_bc` also repeat the `ι W.aᵢ` expansion by hand. The lemma list also skips `baseChange_a₅`, which does not exist, so the pattern is incomplete only in the sense that nothing uses it.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `baseChange_a₁`, `baseChange_a₂`, `baseChange_a₃`, `baseChange_a₄` and `baseChange_a₆` as `@[simp]` (or `@[scoped simp]`). Their right-hand sides contain no `baseChange`, so they cannot loop. Then `hℓ` and `hc` in `descent` should reduce to `simp [Polynomial.map_add, Polynomial.map_mul]`, if `toAffine` unfolds as expected, and `equation_iff_bc` can also use them. If they are not meant to be simp lemmas, delete them as dead code.
findings.benefit: The simp set would handle base-changed coefficients, and the many `(W.baseChange k).toAffine.aᵢ` terms in `descent` would reduce automatically. As written, these lemmas cost reader attention and do nothing.

findings.excerpt: theorem bc_C (x y : k) (p : F[X]) : bc x y (C p) = (p.map ι).eval x := by
findings.problem: The simp set for `bc` is inconsistent. The special cases `bc_CC` (`C (C a)`) and `bc_CX` (`C X`) are `@[scoped simp]`, but the general `bc_C` for `C p` is not. For any other `p`, such as `C (r.coeff 1)` in `exists_bc_eq_linear`, simp does not evaluate `bc x y (C p)` and the proof falls back to `rw [map_add, map_mul, bc_C, bc_C, bc_Y]`. `bc_CC` and `bc_CX` are instances of `bc_C` up to `map_C`, `map_X`, `eval_C` and `eval_X`, so the set is doing the same work in two places.
findings.proposed_change: Either make `bc_C` a `@[scoped simp]` lemma and keep `bc_CC` and `bc_CX` as corollaries, or leave it unmarked and document that it is deliberately manual. If it is marked simp, the normal form for `bc x y (C p)` becomes `(p.map ι).eval x`. That form is further simplified by `Polynomial.map_C`, `eval_C`, `Polynomial.map_X` and `eval_X`, and no cycle is visible.
findings.benefit: The `bc x y` evaluations in `exists_bc_eq_linear` could then be closed by `simp [map_add, map_mul]` instead of a fragile ordered `rw` list. The `bc` simp set would also be uniform.
